findings.title: Backdoored vsftpd 2.3.4
findings.description: The vsftpd 2.3.4 archive was backdoored in 2011 (CVE-2011-2523). A username ending with ":)" opens a root shell on port 6200.
findings.recommendation: Reinstall vsftpd from a trusted source, or replace FTP with SFTP.

findings.title: Telnet in use
findings.description: Telnet sends logins, passwords and commands in cleartext. Anyone on the network path can read them.

findings.title: rexec / rlogin / rsh in use
findings.description: These old remote access services send credentials in cleartext, and rlogin/rsh can trust a client based only on its IP address (.rhosts files).
findings.recommendation: Disable these services and use SSH.

findings.title: Shell open without authentication
findings.description: A command shell is listening on this port. Anyone who connects gets a shell on the machine, without any password.
findings.recommendation: Treat the host as compromised. Isolate it, stop the process and investigate.

findings.title: MySQL account without password
findings.evidence: mysql-empty-password: root account has empty password (checked by riskmap)
findings.description: A MySQL account (often root) accepts a login with an empty password. Anyone on the network can read and modify the data.
findings.recommendation: Set a strong password on every account and remove anonymous accounts.

findings.title: SMBv1 enabled
findings.evidence: smb-protocols: dialects: NT LM 0.12 (SMBv1) [dangerous, but default]
findings.description: SMBv1 is obsolete and insecure. Its Windows implementation was exploited by WannaCry and NotPetya (EternalBlue).
findings.recommendation: Disable SMBv1 (in Samba, "server min protocol = SMB2"; on Windows, remove the SMB 1.0 feature).

findings.title: Anonymous FTP login allowed
findings.evidence: ftp-anon: Anonymous FTP login allowed (FTP code 230)
findings.description: Anyone can log in to the FTP server without an account and read files, sometimes write them.
findings.recommendation: Disable anonymous access unless it is really needed, and never allow anonymous write.

findings.title: Java RMI registry exposed
findings.description: An exposed RMI registry can allow remote code execution when it loads classes from a remote location.
findings.recommendation: Do not expose RMI to the network. Filter the port with a firewall.

findings.title: VNC exposed
findings.description: VNC gives full control of the desktop. It is often protected by a weak password, and the classic protocol does not encrypt the session.
findings.recommendation: Do not expose VNC to the network. Reach it through an SSH tunnel or a VPN.

findings.title: FTP in use (cleartext)
findings.description: FTP sends logins, passwords and files in cleartext.
findings.recommendation: Replace FTP with SFTP or FTPS.

findings.title: Outdated OpenSSH
findings.description: This OpenSSH version is very old and affected by several published vulnerabilities.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade OpenSSH to a supported version.

findings.title: Outdated Apache httpd
findings.description: Apache httpd 2.2 is end of life. Its last release dates from 2017 and it no longer gets security fixes.

findings.title: NFS exposed
findings.description: If the exports are not restricted, any host on the network can mount the shared folders.
findings.recommendation: Restrict /etc/exports to the hosts that need it, or disable NFS.

findings.title: Database reachable over the network
findings.description: The database accepts connections from the network. A database should only be reachable by the applications that use it.
findings.recommendation: Bind the database to localhost or filter the port with a firewall.

findings.title: Outdated MySQL
findings.description: MySQL versions older than 8.0 are end of life and no longer get security fixes.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade MySQL to a supported version.
